extracted.intended_audience: scientists, researchers, and educated readers of Nature (biology, astronomy, physics, botany, geology)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and methodological standards for observing, measuring, classifying, and reporting scientific phenomena across observational astronomy, experimental physics, biology, and natural-history studies as discussed in a Nature news/summary column.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification markers for spirochetes
rubrics_metrics.description: “the diffuse nuclei and transverse fission of spirochates suuggest bacteria, while, on the other hand, the presence of an undulating membrane, longitudinal fission, and even definite 'chromosomes' suggest protozoa.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use morphological and reproductive characters to infer taxonomic status: note diffuse nuclei and transverse fission as evidence favoring bacterial interpretation; undulating membrane, longitudinal fission and apparent chromosomes as evidence favoring protozoan interpretation. Supplement with observations of living behaviour (vibratory flexion for progression; spiral/corkscrew whole-body movement due to spirally wound membrane); note absence of flagella in spirochaetes and that putative flagella may be myoneme fibrils torn from the membrane.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wing-connection development as functional and systematic criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: “Their object is, of course, to enable the two wings to act during flight as a single unit, and, as might have been expected, it turns out that the strongest flyers among the Hymenoptera are those in which the connection between the wings attains its fullest development.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the morphology of wing-linking structures both for functional inference (flight performance) and systematic significance; damaged or reduced connections correlate with halting/uncertain flight and are diagnostically important in comparative/systematic studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental agreement and selection of representative values (e/m measurements)
rubrics_metrics.description: “From the results he calculates by the theory of Lorentz the quotient of the electric charge on the ion by its mass, and obtains 1-79 X10^ . This agrees very well with the value 1-77x10^ given by Messrs. P. Weiss and A. Cotton ... The values which have been obtained by different experimenters for the above quotient in the case of the kathode rays differ so much from each other that it is difficult to fix on a representative one for comparison ...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting fundamental measured quantities, compare with contemporary determinations and discuss discrepancies; acknowledge that different experimental conditions (e.g. different ions) may cause variation, and justify choice of a representative value for comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calibration dependence in high-temperature melting-point determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: “The uncertainty as to the melting point of platinum ... is leading to corresponding uncertainties in all high-temperature determinations. Profs. ... are compelled to give two sets of values, one based on 1745° C, the other on 1789° C, as the melting point of platinum. They use the Nernst glower as a meldometer ... The temperature of the glower is determined by measurement of the isochromatic radiation, assumed to follow a law similar to Wien's, with constants determined from the melting points ...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize and report how derived high-temperature values depend on the choice of calibration standards and assumptions about radiative laws; present alternate result sets when a calibration reference (e.g. platinum melting point) is uncertain, and describe measurement method (device, observation through microscope, isochromatic radiation law) and its calibration chain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size and reagent purity for atomic-weight determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: “Difficulties were encountered owing to the presence of traces of impurities in the reagents, leading to a gradual loss of radium during the purification, and a detailed account is given of the elaborate precautions found to be necessary for the preparation and preservation of the reagents used. ... The atomic weight deduced ... is ... units higher than the value found on 0·09 gram in 1903. It is shown that the slight increase of purity of the 1907 over the 1902 preparation is not sufficient to account for the rise ... the difference being most probably due to the loss of accuracy on the determinations with the smaller quantity and the use of reagents not properly purified.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For precise atomic-weight (or trace-element) work, use sufficiently large sample masses when possible; implement rigorous purification (re-crystallisation from weak HCl, fractional precipitation by alcohol, spectroscopic removal of interfering elements such as barium) and document reagent preparation and storage to prevent systematic losses and contamination; discuss how sample size and reagent purity affect accuracy and differences between determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solar-observation methodology for precise measures
rubrics_metrics.description: “Solar observations were commenced ... In January, 1906, photography was substituted for eye observations for the purpose of obtaining more precise measures, and photographs have since been secured on each clear day. ... a more suitable photoheliograph has recently been erected having an objective of 94 mm. (3·7 inches) aperture and 1·50 m. focal length, and fitted with a direct enlarger giving a solar image of about 10 cm. diameter. The areas and positions of the spots, &c., are measured with a Hilger micrometer, the positions afterwards being reduced to heliocentric coordinates in the usual manner ... Spectroscopic observations ... spectro-photography with a large dispersion will be installed.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt photographic recording over eye observation for higher precision; specify instrument parameters (objective aperture, focal length, image enlargement) and measurement tools (micrometer), and document reduction procedures (conversion to heliocentric coordinates). Plan regular (daily if possible) imaging, publish results at useful frequency for the community, and develop spectro-photographic capability for additional diagnostics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for photographic-variable-star surveys
rubrics_metrics.description: “The wholesale discovery of new variable stars from photographic plates is proceeding ... Prof. Pickering announces the discovery of a further batch of seventy-one new variables ... gives a table showing the proportion of newly discovered variables to the total number now known to exist in each region examined ... The designations, positions, and magnitude ranges of the newly discovered variables are given, and the list includes thirteen probable Algol and seven long-period variables.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct systematic photographic plate surveys, record and publish precise designations, sky positions, and magnitude ranges for each candidate; tabulate discovery rates regionally to estimate completeness (e.g. proportion remaining to be found) and classify variable types (Algol-type, long-period, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Report mean probable errors and include multi-observer measures
rubrics_metrics.description: “Dr. H. E. Lau publishes a further list of Struve double stars measured by himself, and discusses the mean probable errors of his measurements. In addition to the eighty measures made by Dr. Lau, the list also contains twenty-eight measures made by Herr Luplau-Jannsen.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When publishing positional or micrometric measures, compute and report mean probable errors; include and distinguish measurements made by different observers and discuss inter-observer agreement or discrepancies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use cultivation and progeny to test plant-origin hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: “Ordinarily the flowers are white, but a pink-flowered form was introduced ... and recently another plant, bearing rich crimson flowers, has been discovered growing wild. Seedling plants of the latter have been raised, so that from the next generation some idea as to the origin of the plant, whether a mutant or hybrid, may be obtained.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To determine whether an unusual plant form is a mutant or hybrid, raise seedlings and observe the next generation(s) for breeding-true characteristics or segregation patterns; use cultivation and controlled crosses where possible to test origin hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and competency criteria for electrical artisans
rubrics_metrics.description: “The term electrical artisan ... deals almost entirely with those electrical artisans who are generally classified as 'wiremen,' and the paper treats of the possibilities of improving the existing methods in which such men are trained ... there is a very large majority of the 'so-called wiremen' obtaining the maximum rate of wages per hour which the highly trained and competent workman is fully entitled to, who cannot be placed in the same class with him ... This in itself is evidence of the serious defect in the method by which electrical artisans are produced ... until the employers take a practical interest in this matter they cannot hope to obtain the man most suited to their requirements.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess training programs for their ability to produce clearly differentiated competency levels (not merely produce many middling workers). Involve employers practically in designing and sponsoring training so that curricula produce first-class artisans suited to industrial requirements and avoid wage/skill mismatches.
